Favourite Hero?

 

A lot of people seem to have favourite heroes.

Lots of people are wrong.

Liking an individual hero misses the point for me.

Of course I have heroes that I want to play more than others, but only when I am in specific moods,

For instance if I am mentally tired I want a low complexity hero.

The way the group of heroes interact with each other is more important to me then an individual hero's personality.

Having them all be my favourites means I don't have a least favourite!

Everyone is awesome!

Maybe this is a cop out but it's how I feel!

 

Favourite Non-Vengance Villain?

 

Hey! Why do you have to discriminate like that?

Even the Vengeance villains need love!

Realistically though, how I can choose a favourite villain without the others getting angry I didn't pick them?

One doesn't have a villain proof bunker one could hide in!

I guess I'll just have to pick one that isn't really a villain

Consider the fact that this villain is only a villain because the shard "chose" him for the ego part of the power

In an alternate reality Nigel is the hero and Hugh is the villain!

Not even the power of OblivAeon was able to overcome his sense of Justice though

For eventually he returned to his senses (albeit briefly) and helped the heroes

It's what he was trained to do as a policeman, to keep the peace

Not to enforce it as a hero-turn-dictator might do

It is an uplifting story that despite all that happened to him his last act was one of self-sacrifice

Touching, that his brother has a permanent reminder of what Nigel really was underneath it all

OblivAeon shall pay for his death

(Really it's just because he's British though)

“Voss’ flagship is almost in range!” Tachyon, team leader, warned the heroes from the Freedom Tower command center. “The torpedo tubes are open; he’ll be launching the Gene-Shaper Warhead the moment he’s able.”

“Kinda busy here,” grunted The Wraith, dispatching another two Gene-Bound Lancers with her razor ordinance.

“I’m on my way, team!” Legacy radioed.

“You might not get there fast enough,” Tachyon said. “The Conqueror is approaching the orbit of the International Space Station, and I calculate the weapon launch point as…forty-two seconds before you arrive.”

“I’ll push harder!” vowed Legacy, the sound of his cape snapping in the wind in the background.

“Not good enough.” Tachyon set her jaw. “Tyler, can you get your NASA buddies on the line?”

“On it.”

A moment passed as the fight against the Gene-Bound army raged through the streets of Megalopolis. Tachyon took advantage of the moment between radio calls to scarf down a pizza and replenish her energy stores.

“They’re on it,” Vance radioed from the Bunker suit. “An astronaut is in the Phoenix spacecraft. It’s Joe.”

“I see it separating from the station now,” replied Tachyon. “What’s his plan?”

“One-way trip, I think,” Vance said, grimly.

At that moment, Tachyon’s display showed the spacecraft begin a hard burn, moving toward the Conqueror. Smaller blips appeared, streaking towards the human craft.

“Incoming missiles!” Tachyon shouted.

Legacy yelled, struggling to put on a burst of speed as the missiles closed in.

A series of quick bursts fired from the Phoenix’s maneuvering jets and the capsule darted sideways, avoiding the Thorathian weapons.

“He’s safe! It’s like he knew the missiles’ trajectory!” exclaimed Tachyon.

The little human spacecraft jumped laterally again, narrowly avoiding laser fire from the Conqueror’s forward batteries.

“What’s going on?” Bunker asked, grenading a passing Gene-Bound Shock Trooper.

“Yee-ow!” Tachyon cried. “He’s dodging every - uh, oh.”

“Uh-oh?” Wraith demanded. “What’s ‘uh-oh,’ Stimson?!”

“Conqueror just passed the red line. It can - there it goes! THE GENETIC WARHEAD IS AWAY!”

The heroes held their collective breath as Grand Warlord Voss’ weapon of mass gene-engineering blasted along a corkscrewing, erratic course towards Megalopolis. The Phoenix tumbled about and the capsule’s thrusters sputtered, jetting it towards the maneuvering warhead. The distance closed rapidly.

“I’m almost there!” Legacy said. “Just another–”

A brilliant flash blinded Tachyon’s tactical displays as the capsule collided with Voss’ villainous device. Streamers of radiant blue energy crackled out into the upper atmosphere. They redshifted as they stretched out, slowly fading into invisibility. The explosion left only a crumpled wreck of the NASA space capsule, falling into the stratosphere. A red-white-and-blue costumed figure zoomed in toward the broken hull.

“You’re clear, Legacy,” called Tachyon. “I’m reading negative gene warhead emissions.”

“I’ve got him,” Legacy radioed back. “Somehow he survived the explosion, but he’s unconscious.”

“We can take care of the ground forces,” Bunker declared. “Tachyon, you want to get an isolation unit ready?”

“Sure, good idea - okay, all done. Legacy, bring him back here.”

So, yeah. I’m a spacecraft engineer, and my work involves pointing spacecraft in the right direction and maneuvering their orbits around. But when I signed up for this forum, I also wanted a superhero-y name. Thus, TRAJECTOR was born!

Trajector:

@grysqrl - Where and why did you learn metalworking?

Why? Because I like to make things. I've been a hobby woodworker for about a decade and like to incorporate multiple materials in my projects, whenever possible. Several years back, I did a little work for Miller Electric (they make TIG welders); I was already interested in metalworking, but working on that project gave me a good push to learn more.

Where? I had a hard time finding places to learn metalworking as a hobby; I mostly encountered certification training for professional welders, which wasn't really what I wanted. I happened to find an art center in a nearby suburb that had a metalworking department. I took a couple of classes and was hooked. The art center has moved to a new building that can't accommodate metalworking, so the guy that running the show there broke off and founded the Chicago Industrial Arts and Design Center. I helped get it set up and have been working there ever since.

~28 years ago, I was a sophomore in college, and I got up one Saturday morning (after a long Friday evening of D&D) and sat down at a computer to play a game called (Classic) Empire.

The next thing I knew, it was midnight and I hadn't done anything else except go to the bathroom. I hadn't eaten all day.

That was when I realized I needed to not play computer games. Over the years, I've made a few exceptions, such as Portal (because it's Portal – seriously, awesome game!) and being a beta-tester for Handelabra's Sentinels, but I just don't play computer games anymore. I like my life, and I'd rather not miss out on it.

Plus, just bought a house that has turned out to need more work than planned, so funds are a little tight…

So, to directly answer your question, nothing.

My apologies that it's a boring answer.
